tagline: Out of Heavener and down the Ouachita valleys to Arkansas.
intro: US 59 and 270 leave Heavener and wind 22 miles through the forested valleys of the Ouachita Mountains and the Winding Stair Mountain National Recreation Area to the Arkansas line. It is a two-lane paved road with steep grades and sharp curves, and its hills climb to nearly 2,600 feet.
This was timber country once, and sawmills came and went along it. Side roads lead off into the heavily forested mountains, and wilderness areas lie alongside the byway.

moments.title: Heavener
moments.text: When the railroad came through in 1896 the town's first post office opened in a boxcar, and another boxcar served as the train station.

moments.title: Stapp
moments.text: A lumber town of about 1,000 at its height, its sawmill closed in 1932 after cutting and moving on, and nothing of the old town remains.

moments.title: Page
moments.text: Five and a half miles short of Arkansas, Page took its name in 1896 from William C. Page, a prominent Choctaw.
